title: Statistical Canary Gate: chi-squared A/B divergence detector with auto-rollback
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a statistically grounded canary gate that compares categorical quality distributions between baseline and rollout cohorts using a chi-squared divergence test. The gate will operate for both Canary and A/B rollout modes, enforce minimum sample sizes and effect-size detection, and automatically trigger an orchestrated rollback when a statistically significant degradation is observed. This complements existing metric-based evals by focusing on distributional shifts in discrete quality labels (e.g., OK/WEAK/FAIL) and structured output mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Canary gate computes chi-squared statistic and p-value for configured categorical metrics every evaluation window
AC2: Minimum sample size enforcement prevents gating on low-traffic cohorts (configurable threshold per project)
AC3: Auto-rollback trigger executes orchestrated rollback plan when p-value < alpha and effect size exceeds configured phi threshold
AC4: Gate emits event to tracing/logging with evaluation provenance: baseline cohort id, variant cohort id, sample counts, chi2, p-value, bucket counts
AC5: All gate decisions appear in Console rollouts UI within 30s of decision with playbook link and suggested next steps
AC6: Integration tests simulate synthetic regressions and the rollback workflow completes end-to-end in staging
implementation_notes: Create new evaluation worker that accepts binned categorical metrics (schema: metric_name, buckets[], counts[])
Implement chi-squared computation library with Yates continuity correction option; expose significance alpha and min_n as config
Extend rollout controller to register gates and subscribe to gate verdict events; add rollback orchestration hook that preserves request routing state
Add config entry in model-config for 'stat_canary' with parameters: metric_list, alpha, min_n, phi_effect_size, hysteresis_windows
Instrument telemetry: gate_evaluation{metric,baseline_n,variant_n,chi2,p_value,verdict} and a rollback_executed event with reason and operator
Coordinate with Console team to add verdict card and link to playbook; define UX copy and severity tags
test_plan: Unit tests for chi-squared math across edge cases (zero counts, sparse buckets)
Integration test: synthetic shift where variant increases FAIL bucket by 5% and gate triggers rollback
Load test: evaluation worker can process 5k cohort comparisons/min with 95th pct latency < 300ms
Staging run: enable gate on internal-only org with 1% traffic for 48h and validate no false positives
Chaos test: simulate delayed metrics and ensure hysteresis prevents flip-flop rollbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'stat_canary' – enable evaluation mode only (no auto-rollback) for 1 week on internal org
Phase 1: Enable verdict logging and Console card, run on 1% traffic for 48h, manual operator review required
Phase 2: Enable auto-rollback for non-prod with low severity thresholds at 5% traffic
Phase 3: Progressive ramp to 20% then 100% for controlled customers with SLA waiver; monitor for 2 weeks
Rollback playbook: automated route revert -> notify on-call -> open RCA ticket template in Console
comments: 2025-01-10 Priya Nair: Initial ticket created after spike of silent regressions in structured output tests. Motivation: distributional checks caught earlier in offline evals would have prevented two incidents in Q4.
2025-01-12 Miguel Alvarez: Drafted design and simulation harness. Decided to use chi-squared for categorical buckets rather than KL divergence to preserve ease of interpretation for PMs.

2025-01-15 Design review (Sara Patel): UX wants a single verdict card with confidence interval and suggestion button to open a canary replay; requested time-series of bucket proportions in the Console card.
2025-01-18 Engineering sync: trade-off discussion—Yates correction reduces false positives on small buckets but can mask real shifts; we will make correction configurable per-metric.

2025-01-20 Data science note (Liu Chen): Ran offline backtests on 6 months of rollout data. At alpha=0.01 and phi=0.03 we detected 14/16 historical regressions with 2 false positives (acceptable). Attached results in Confluence.
2025-01-22 Security review: no PII in bucket counts; telemetry will send only aggregated counts. Confirmed with security that KMS keys are not required for gate events.
2025-01-24 QA: Created synthetic test harness and found an edge-case where zero-count buckets cause NaN; added guard to collapse zero-count-only buckets before test.
2025-01-26 Miguel Alvarez: Opened WIP PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-safety/pull/289). Unit tests added. Moving to integration testing in CI-staging.

2025-01-28 Priya Nair: Product sign-off on thresholds for Canary internal run. Next steps: Console card mockups accepted, schedule 1% internal canary for 2025-02-03. Follow-up ticket to add multi-metric aggregation is needed.
notes: We intentionally choose a generative-agnostic approach: chi-sq works on labeled outputs and can be applied to model-generated classes or eval rubric buckets.
Future work: extend gate to continuous metrics using Kolmogorov–Smirnov or two-sample t-tests and combine multi-metric evidence with weighted scoring
Operational concern: avoid noisy rollbacks at low traffic—hysteresis window and min_n must be tuned per customer cohort
